meaning: Expected annual loss: long-run average; the right basis for budgeting and cost-benefit of controls.
Monte Carlo standard error of the EAL estimate (s / sqrt(N)).
A typical year. Far below the EAL for skewed losses: most years are cheap, a few are very expensive.
Loss exceeded one year in four.
Loss exceeded one year in ten.
Loss exceeded one year in twenty; a common planning / appetite anchor.
Loss exceeded one year in a hundred.
Value at Risk at 95 %: same number as P95, stated as a capital/contingency level.
Expected shortfall at 95 %: average of the worst 5 % of years; captures how bad the tail is, not just where it starts.
Expected shortfall at 99 %: average of the worst 1 % of years; sensitive to major-accident severity.
Largest simulated year: depends mostly on sample size; an indicator, not a risk measure.
